## 2026-11-07 - The pirate's hat in geometry nodes (Blender look-dev, 30-minute task)
- Asked: a new .blend recreating the pirate's hat with geometry nodes, as close to the pirate sprite
  as possible, in at most 30 minutes (took about 12).
- Done: external/blender/pirate_hat/build_hat.py builds pirate_hat.blend from an empty file: one
  object "PirateHat" whose geometry all comes from the "PirateHat" node tree (207 nodes): the brim
  (a 241 x 14 Grid in angle / across space bent into a surface of revolution - a ledge out from the
  crown, then walls leaning out; outline drawn out to three points that flick up, back walls a bit
  higher; extruded 8 mm), the crown (squashed, raised UV sphere) and a dark band, a gold trim (the
  brim's edge as a curve swept by a circle) with 22 gold spikes and balls on the points, gold hooks on
  the front points, a skull and crossbones on the front wall. Materials: leather (noise bump), gold,
  bone, dark sockets. Previews: front / q45 / side / back renders and preview_vs_reference.png.
- Tried and dropped: a two-wall (bicorne-like) reading of the sprite - came out as a bowl.
- Not in the game: the sprites still come from the Tripo model; the hat is a standalone model.
- Files: new external/blender/pirate_hat/ (build_hat.py, pirate_hat.blend, preview_*.png)
- Then (asked: the reference hat has four sides, not three): POINTS_AT = four corners (45 / 135 / 225 /
  315 deg) - front, back, left and right walls; corners flick up 70 mm, walls flare 45 mm, and the whole
  hat is scaled 1.14 x 0.94 (wider than deep, like the sprite's). The brim formula takes any number of
  points.
- Then (asked: the front and back should be more like triangles): the front and back walls rise to a
  peak in the middle (PEAK 85 mm, straight edges - linear in x), the side walls stay level; base walls
  85 / 100 mm, corners flick up 30 mm; the skull sits in the front triangle.
- Then (asked: a much more realistic skull on the front): skull_unit() sculpts it with signed-distance
  grids (Mesh to SDF Grid, voxel 0.018 skull widths): cranium, brow ridge, face, cheekbones and their
  arches, lower jaw, chin and jaw corners unioned and filleted; eye sockets (rounded squares, tilted
  out), the nose (two leaning lobes - an upside-down heart), the gap between the jaws, the hollows under
  the cheekbones and the temples carved out (SDF difference); Grid to Mesh (threshold 0 - the default
  0.1 gives nothing for a distance field). 16 teeth in two arcs (front ones longer), dark hollows deep
  in the sockets and nose. Bone material: noise ivory-to-yellowed, multiplied by ambient occlusion
  (darker crevices), a slight bump. The crossbones' ends got double knobs. preview_skull.png: a close-up.
- Then (asked: no spikes - slime dripping down from the top edges instead): the spikes are gone. Slime
  (green, wet, a little see-through, faintly glowing): a lumpy band along the top edges (the edge curve
  swept with a noise radius 6-12 mm) and drips from about 40% of 64 points along it - each a tapering
  stem bent down the wall's outer face (a line resampled and set onto the brim formula at lower
  `across`, per-drip angle / length / thickness stored as attributes) with a bulb at its end; all
  unioned through a filleted distance field (1.6 mm voxels) so drips flow out of the band. Drips stay on
  the upright part of the wall and sit wholly outside it (first tries ran onto the brim's inside / cut
  through the single-sheet wall - checked with ray casts).
- Then (asked: a drip ran through the skull - it should run over it): every drip point (the stems,
  now 28 points each, and the bulbs) is raycast straight in from outside against the skull and
  crossbones; where they're further out than the drip, it's set just outside where the ray meets them,
  so the drip flows over the skull's face. Built live in the user's Blender (from now on: they watch).
- Then (asked: a gold-like colour for the slime): liquid gold - colour (0.95, 0.6, 0.1), half metallic
  (0.55), roughness 0.12, less see-through (transmission 0.1), a fainter glow (0.25).

## 2026-11-07 - A new gun ("AAD-73") modelled in geometry nodes from ~/Downloads/gun2.png
- Asked: model the rifle in gun2.png (a side view) in a new .blend, with geometry nodes, as one model,
  as close to the reference as possible.
- Done: external/blender/gun2/build_gun.py (run headless) builds gun2.blend: one object "Gun" whose
  geometry all comes from the "Gun" node tree. Laid out on the reference's pixels (0.5 mm a pixel - the
  gun is about 0.75 m long; muzzle -X, the shown side faces -Y). Flat parts are polygons traced off the
  reference (a Curve Circle with a point per corner, set from an Index Switch, filled, extruded, capped);
  the receiver, stock, grip and magazine are rounded through a distance field (eroded and grown back
  3.5-4 mm); the muzzle shroud's bore and slots are carved out of it (SDF difference). Round parts:
  shroud, bands, copper barrel housing, the glass energy cell with a bright yellow core, top rod and
  clamps, under-barrel rail with lugs; the scope (bells, tube, rings, lenses, turrets, mount). Details:
  the window with six cyan charge segments, the "AAD-73" plate (String to Curves, filled, extruded) in a
  dark frame, hazard stripes, raised side panels, rivets, the knob, the bolt block, the trigger guard (a
  filled outline with its hole), the trigger and front lever (swept curves), the skull-and-octopus
  emblem on the stock, three drips of molten gold from the rail. Materials: worn maroon paint, copper,
  dark gunmetal, brass, rubber (two noise masks: rust patches and dark chips, rough where worn), glass,
  the two glows, gold.
- Found: Blender's Mesh Cone primitive runs from its base at 0 to +depth (not centred, unlike the
  Cylinder); GN Extrude Mesh drops the original faces (slabs get their back face re-added, flipped).
- Previews: external/blender/gun2/preview_{side,q3,rear,top}.png and preview_vs_reference.png.
- Not in the game (the pirate still holds the Tripo gun).
- Files: new external/blender/gun2/ (build_gun.py, gun2.blend, previews)
- Second pass (asked: closer to the reference): materials get pitting (Voronoi spots, denser on the
  grip's rubber), wear is mostly dark chips over the paint (smaller, 70 / m), copper warmer, the scope
  its own dark bronze; scope detail (engraved plates on the bells and tube, a knurled ring of 16 studs
  on the side turret, two more brass rims); the magazine's label plate and brass base edge; dark steel
  strips on the butt's edge and the stock's lower chamfer; a bolder emblem (bigger skull, thicker
  tentacles); lighting warm key / pink rim / dim top over a darker purple; bloom in the compositor
  (Glare: Bloom, threshold 2.5 - only the glowing lights). (Blender 5 compositing: a CompositorNodeTree
  node group set as scene.compositing_node_group, Render Layers -> Glare -> Group Output.)
- Then (asked: the octopus sign must be close to the reference): the emblem is now traced from the
  reference itself inside the node tree - the image is packed into gun2.blend; a grid over the emblem
  (4 points a reference pixel, 118 x 105 px) samples it (GN Image Texture), keeps cells whose linear
  colour is the gold paint (red > 0.3, green > 0.11 - the maroon has green ~0.01, the orange rust ~0.09),
  drops separate pieces under 600 cells (specks), extrudes 1.3 mm onto the stock's panel and smooths the
  stair-stepped edge through a distance field (0.18 mm voxels). preview_emblem.png: a close-up.
- Then (asked: break it into objects in a collection, grouped to move as one; and the triangle count):
  every piece the node tree makes is tagged with a "part" face attribute (31 part() markers in build());
  split_parts() turns the evaluated mesh into one object per part - 25: Receiver, Stock, Grip, Magazine,
  Trigger guard, Trigger, Front lever, Charge window, Name plate, Hazard stripes, Side panels, Rivets, Knob,
  Bolt block, Emblem, Muzzle shroud, Barrel bands, Barrel housing, Energy cell, Top rod, Rod clamps,
  Under-barrel rail, Scope, Scope mount, Gold drips - each with its origin at its middle and only its own
  materials, in the collection "AAD-73", parented to the empty "AAD-73" (move that, the gun follows). The
  procedural object is kept in a hidden collection "AAD-73 (procedural)". Total 663,612 triangles (332,026
  vertices); the distance-field parts are most of it: emblem 163k, shroud 149k, receiver 130k, stock 81k,
  grip 54k, magazine 47k, drips 31k; everything else ~9k.

## 2026-11-07 - Sound effects: the pirate's (the game's first audio)
- Asked: analyse and generate audio effects for the pirate.
- Found: the game had no audio at all - no sound files, no players, no volume setting.
- Made: tools/sfx_pirate.py synthesises them from scratch with numpy (oscillators with pitch sweeps,
  filtered noise, inharmonic metal partials, a formant "voice" - a buzz through vowel resonances,
  ring-modulated and bit-crushed into a robot; seeded, so the same takes every run) and writes
  sounds/pirate/*.ogg (Vorbis q5, mono 44.1 kHz): 31 takes, 392 KB - shot x4 (falling zap, crack,
  thump; 0.42 s), raise x2 / lower x2 (servo whir with gear flutter, then a click / clunk), step x6
  (thud and a short clank), hurt x4 (sizzle and a robotic grunt), death x2 (falling whine, sparks, a
  crash and a bounce; 1.9 s), taunt x4 (a growled robot babble of 3-5 syllables ending in a rolled
  "arr"), flee x2 (alarm chirps and a quick higher babble), bolt_hit x3, loot_drop, loot_take.
- Analysis (also external/sfx/pirate_analysis.md and pirate_spectrograms.png): every take checked for
  peak, loudest-100-ms level, crest, spectral centroid, low-end share and start/end clicks (none). It
  caught three problems, fixed: the hurt grunt was buried under the sizzle (formant resonators left the
  voice ~20 dB down: now normalised), raise too quiet (-22.6 -> -13.9 dBFS), flee too loud (-7 ->
  -14.4). Levels now: shots / hurt / taunts / bolt hits ~-12..-17 dBFS loud, footsteps ~-18, death -9.
- Game: scripts/sfx.gd, a new autoload "Sfx": play_at(key, pos, parent) (AudioStreamPlayer2D - fades
  with distance from the camera, 1500 px, falloff 1.6) and play(key) (flat), a random take each time at
  +-6 % pitch, at most 6 of one sound and 40 in all at once, all on an "SFX" bus. Settings.sfx_volume
  (saved under [audio]) with a "Sound effects" slider in the menu's Settings (plays a sample shot as
  you move it; Restore Defaults puts it back to 100%).
- Hooks: SurfacePirate - its shots, the rifle raised / lowered (_go), footsteps (each half walk cycle),
  hurt (not within 0.3 s of the last), death, taunt (clicking it), flee; LaserBolt - a pirate's bolt
  striking; PlanetSurface - the loot chest dropping, and taking it. The Library's pirate plays them too.
- Tests: test_surface.test_pirate_sounds (every take loads and is short, unknown sounds are silent, the
  SFX bus, the per-sound cap, the volume setting / mute, a pirate firing / raising / hurt / falling is
  heard). All tests 65 passed.
- Docs: game.md (Pirates: what you hear; the Sound effects volume).
- Files: new scripts/sfx.gd, tools/sfx_pirate.py, sounds/pirate/*.ogg (31) and their .import files,
  external/sfx/; changed project.godot (autoload), scripts/settings.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd,
  scripts/surface_props.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, tests/test_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md

## 2026-11-07 - Economy: narrowing the gap between trading and fighting
- Asked: an economy report (no change), then "implement 4" - its fix 4: trading paid 25-35x more
  than fighting (a 60-unit home-system haul ~2,500-4,000 cr vs ~110 cr for a pirate fighter).
- Market footprint (Galaxy): every unit you buy at a station pushes its price up 0.3 %
  (PLAYER_IMPACT, compounding), every unit you sell pushes it down - up to 2x as hard on goods the
  station is short of (IMPACT_SCARCE); it fades 1.5 % per 2 s economy tick (IMPACT_DECAY: 22 % off
  after a 60-unit sale -> 14 % after 90 s, 3 % after 5 min). Stored per station ("impact", saved).
  NPC traders see it too. Measured on the best home routes after 20 min: 20-unit loads keep 84-90 %
  of their old profit, 60-unit hauls dumped at one station 19-59 % (one already-thin route goes
  slightly negative) - spreading a hold over stations pays. Tried 0.6 % first: full hauls lost money.
- Bounties: Galaxy.pirate_bounty(hull, shields) = (hull + shields) x 1.0 + 60 (was x 0.35 + 25):
  interceptor 51 -> 135, fighter 60 -> 160, gunship 92 -> 250, frigate 130 -> 360 (still x1.6 in
  Pirate Raids, + rank bonus). Pirate Sweep missions 70 -> 140 cr per kill. A fighter kill is now
  ~205 cr + items; trading is ~3-5x combat instead of 25-35x.
- UI: market Buy 10 / Sell all tooltips explain the footprint. Docs: game.md (trading, bounties).
- Tests: test_galaxy.test_player_market_footprint (push, fade, scarcity, save, bounty). 72 passed.
- Files: scripts/galaxy.gd, main.gd, missions.gd, station_menu.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_galaxy.gd

## 2026-11-07 - Economy: ending the permanent shortage, and the starting-ship trade-in
- Asked: "fix 1 and 2" from the economy report.
- Fix 1, the shortage (Galaxy). Measured before: 30 % of station stocks at 0 for good, food at 0 in
  34 of 38 stations, median chain efficiency 0.25 (the floor), median price 1.42x base. Causes and
  changes, each measured with a 2-hour headless run:
  1. More used than made galaxy-wide (food 12 made vs 34 used): ECONOMIES rebalanced so every good
     is made at least as fast as it's used (food 28 vs 23, water 18 vs 13, fuel 22.5 vs 18.4,
     platinum 4.8 vs 4.4...); war demand 1.6 -> 1.3 (WAR_DEMAND). Alone: barely helped (28 %).
  2. Starved stations kept consuming: consumption now x (0.5 + 0.5 x input efficiency).
  3. Traders could carry ~10-15 units/s, stations used ~110: RATE 0.5 -> 0.1 per rate unit (all
     production / consumption, and state demand), trader waits 12-35 s -> 5-15 s. 28 % -> 14 %.
  4. Traders hauled only dear goods (food margin ~14 cr vs ~80 for luxuries): supply contracts in
     _plan_trade - a good the destination uses and is short of counts for an extra
     (2 x value + 25) x shortage per unit (NEED_PREMIUM, NEED_FLAT); unprofitable legs skipped.
  5. Geography: the home cluster and all of Ionia had no farm. A generated system's second station
     is now a staples station (farm / mine / refinery), in turn through each empire's STAPLES list
     (the rng call is kept, so station names and places don't move); 4 -> 10 farms.
  6. Goods a station neither makes nor uses rest at 100 (= base price), not 40 (1.42x).
  After: 7 % of stocks at 0 (a quarter of them the two pirate dens, which traders never visit), food
  at 0 in 4 stations, median efficiency 0.73-0.90, median price 1.00x base. Best home-system trades

## 2026-11-07 - Robot voices for the characters (text to speech, numpy-made)
- Asked: text to speech; of the three options offered (Piper neural voices, Godot's OS speech,
  robot voices made from scratch) the user chose the robot voices, maybe Piper later.
- tools/voice_gen.py (numpy only, seeded): source-filter synthesis - a buzz / narrow pulse through
  three vowel formants (a e i o u), and consonant kinds (p burst, b voiced burst, s hiss, f soft
  hiss, h breath, m nasal hum, l liquid, w glide) - each at 3 pitches (-3, 0, +4 semitones) = 39
  sounds per voice, then the voice's colour: ring modulation (metallic), bit-crush + sample-hold,
  a radio band (380-3000 Hz, saturated), a sub-harmonic growl; a 5.2 kHz low-pass tames the
  crushing's fizz (energy above 5 kHz 23-37 dB down). Levelled by vowel RMS (-14 dBFS, soft
  limiter: the nine voices within 1 dB). 9 voices: kilon (92 Hz, pulse, ring 61 Hz, crushed),
  ariadne (205 Hz, clean), daidalos (118 Hz), asterion (78 Hz, growl), talos (64 Hz, heavy ring),
  narrator (108 Hz, clean), radio (stations), citizen, pirate. -> voices/<voice>.wav (16-bit PCM,
  22050 Hz, imported uncompressed: compress/mode=0) + .json index; 1.3 MB in all.
- Voice autoload (scripts/voice.gd): speak(text, speaker[, voice]) / stop(); a line becomes its
  letters' sounds (BBCode stripped, doubled letters once), 45 ms between words, 170 ms at commas,
  330 ms at full stops; melody: long words' first vowel high, a statement's last word falls, a
  question's rises. Assembled as one AudioStreamWAV (slices of the bank, no per-sample work), on the
  new "Voice" bus, playing while paused. ~13 characters a second (a 111-character line: 8 s).
  Speakers -> voices (SPEAKERS; stations -> radio; anyone else -> citizen). Any line, edited or new,
  is spoken without regenerating.
- The dialogue box speaks each line in its speaker's voice and stops when it moves on / closes; the
  comms window (hails, citizens face to face) speaks too (pirates growl, citizens, else radio).
- Settings: a 4th volume, "Voices" (Voice bus, default 80 %), a slider in Settings (moving it,
  Kilon says a few words).
- Analysis: external/voices/analysis.md, demo.ogg (one story line per voice, 292 KB),
  demo_spectrograms.png.
- Tests: test_audio.test_robot_voices (banks, voices per speaker, the script: BBCode, doubles,
  pauses, rising / falling, lengths; the dialogue box speaks per speaker and stops); volume tests
  with the Voices bus / slider. 78 passed.
- Docs: game.md (Sound: robot voices, the Voices volume).
- Files: new tools/voice_gen.py, scripts/voice.gd, voices/*.wav (9) + .json (9) + .import,
  external/voices/; changed project.godot (autoload Voice), scripts/settings.gd, main_menu.gd,
  dialogue.gd, comms.gd, tests/test_audio.gd, data/docs/game.md

## 2026-11-08 - Following a ship: smooth, at its speed
- Asked: following an NPC ship moved your ship in repetitive move-and-stop steps; it should be one
  continuous motion matching the followed ship's speed.
- Cause: following re-aimed at a point behind it only past 1.25 x the distance and stopped inside
  0.9 x, and each aim used the arrive-and-brake steering - so you braked, stopped, fell behind, went
  again.
- Ship._follow_velocity: your desired velocity = its velocity + a proportional catch-up (x1.4)
  toward the slot FOLLOW_DIST (260) behind it (behind its heading when it moves, else on your side),
  capped at your top speed; the ship turns to face where it's going (or the other ship when still)
  and accelerates smoothly (velocity.move_toward). No arriving, no stopping.
- Test: test_play.test_follow_is_smooth - following a ship cruising at 180: after catching up, for
  6 s your speed stays within 20 % of its speed (no stops, no racing ahead) and the gap within 60 of
  260.
- Files: scripts/ship.gd, tests/test_play.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Fix: following a hovering ship swung you back and forth
- Reported: following an NPC ship you got stuck going back and forth over a short distance in
  empty space.
- Cause: the slot you kept was "behind its heading" when it moved faster than 20, else "on your
  side" - a ship hovering or drifting slowly crossed that line again and again, flipping the slot
  to its other side each time; you also matched its little jitters.
- Fix (Ship._follow_velocity): a persistent bearing to the slot (_follow_dir, set on follow) that
  swings round behind it only while it's really travelling (> FOLLOW_TRAVEL 70) and only gradually
  (FOLLOW_TURN 0.9 rad/s); you match its velocity only while it travels; within FOLLOW_SLACK 40 of
  the slot no correction (hold station), beyond it an easing (x1.2) toward it.
- Test: test_play.test_follow_a_hovering_ship - a ship drifting +-35 px/s around one spot for 15 s:
  you moved 1909 px in 10 s before (failed), now under 500 with at most 6 reversals and still about
  260 behind it; test_follow_is_smooth and the click test still pass.

## 2026-11-08 - The Minoan armchair: chairs in the buildings from a sprite sheet
- Asked: use the new isometric sheet of a Minoan chair (Downloads) for the chairs in the buildings,
  scale it correctly, and say whether its camera angle is right.
- The sheet (external/images/minoan_chair_sheet.png, 1536 x 1024): 8 views, 2 x 4, on a smooth
  brown-to-purple backdrop with glows - not a flat colour. tools/cut_soft_sheet.py (new): the backdrop
  is what's smooth (low local contrast) and connected to the cell's border through smooth pixels;
  the rest is the object; a pixel of feather; edge pixels tinted by the backdrop (the purple floor
  glow) fade out. Its eight views are two near-duplicate pairs (two front three-quarter views, two
  back ones) - no side views; the four the game needs: se (faces down-right), sw, ne, nw (the two
  front 3/4 labels were swapped on the first pass and fixed). -> art/furniture/chair_{se,sw,ne,nw}.png,
  124 px tall, mipmapped, drawn at half size.
- Scale: characters are 122 px ~ 1.8 m (~68 px / m): the armchair (~0.9 m) CHAIR_H 62 px; the table
  raised to TABLE_H 48 px (~0.75 m; was 30, below the chair's arms). A cell is only ~1 m at this
  scale, so a table now has one chair pulled up to it (facing it: nw / ne views) instead of two
  side by side; a lone chair faces into the room with its back to the wall (se / sw). A soft
  shadow under it.
- The camera angle (told the user): the yaw is right (about 45 degrees), the projection near
  orthographic (legs vertical) - but the camera is too low: the game's 2:1 tiles are a ~30 degree
  elevation (floor edges at 26.6 degrees), the chair's floor-level edges run at 19-22 degrees and
  its seat looks very shallow from the front - about 20 degrees. At 62 px it reads fine, but a
  re-render at 30 degrees elevation would sit exactly on the floor grid.
- Tests: test_furniture checks the four chair pictures. 91 passed. Screenshot: a palace table with
  its chair.
- Files: new tools/cut_soft_sheet.py, art/furniture/chair_*.png (4) + .import (mipmaps),
  external/images/minoan_chair_sheet.png; changed scripts/furniture.gd, tests/test_surface.gd
